result.request: Fictional enterprise scenario: A sponsor requests a guaranteed five-minute HireRight screening-status update in the recruiting system. API access, destination capabilities, and delivery timing have not been tested. Can we promise this? Investigate the evidence and recommend the next validation step.

assessment.summary: No—five-minute status visibility in the recruiting system cannot be promised. HireRight documentation supports a push approach to a client HTTPS endpoint, but neither customer access/configuration nor destination-system receipt, processing, display behavior, or timing has been tested. Because the requirement is change-to-display, end-to-end measurement must begin at HireRight’s actual status-change time; without a trustworthy source-event time, the five-minute outcome cannot be established.
assessment.endpoint: A customer-provided HTTPS endpoint for HireRight status pushes is the candidate delivery path. A documented status lookup, GET /orders/{id}/status, may support reconciliation for a known order but does not establish timely delivery or display.
assessment.expectedResult: Validation should produce evidence that a status change is pushed, acknowledged, processed by the recruiting integration, and visibly updated in the recruiting system within five minutes measured from the vendor status-change time—not merely from message receipt.

evidence.claim: HireRight recommends pushing status updates to a client HTTPS endpoint; a successful HTTP acknowledgement only signals receipt, and redelivery is optional and requires configuration.
HireRight documents GET /orders/{id}/status for retrieving an order summary with order, adjudication, and product statuses; the endpoint has not been executed for this customer.

unknowns: Whether the sponsor has enabled/configured HireRight push updates, including redelivery, and has credentials and a non-production test setup.
Whether the recruiting system exposes an integration endpoint and can process, persist, and visibly display the relevant status update.
The actual delivery, downstream processing, retry, and display latencies under representative conditions.
Whether a trustworthy HireRight status-change timestamp is available to measure vendor-change-to-display timing.
Which status constitutes the requested business update; an order completion/status signal must not be treated as hiring clearance.
assessment.nextTest: The sponsor’s HireRight integration administrator and recruiting-system technical owner should jointly run one non-production status-change test after confirming push configuration and a reachable HTTPS receiver. Capture the vendor’s authoritative status-change time (if available), receiver arrival and acknowledgement times, integration processing time, and the recruiting-system visible-update time. Expected evidence: an end-to-end timestamped trace showing the selected status reaches visible display within five minutes, plus behavior for a failed acknowledgement/redelivery scenario. If no trustworthy source-event time is available, record that only receipt-to-display latency was measured and do not claim the five-minute end-to-end guarantee.
questions: Can the sponsor provide non-production HireRight access/configuration and a recruiting-system technical owner with a reachable test endpoint?
What exact screening status must be displayed, and is there an authoritative vendor status-change timestamp available for measurement?
